value.lexeme:
>-
      A continuously derived quality that emerges from patterns
      of Events between Entities. Aligned with BFO:Specifically
      Dependent Continuant (Quality) and SSN/SOSA:Observation.
      A Signal inheres in its bearer(s) — it does not exist
      independently. It is computed, not asserted: derived on
      demand from the Event log and Entity graph via a named
      algorithm. Domain projects define signal types, algorithms,
      and interpretation semantics. The Signal class captures
      the universal pattern: something measurable that emerges
      from activity, has a current value, and is recomputable
      from the underlying data.
value.value: A continuously derived quality that emerges from patterns of Events between Entities. Aligned with BFO:Specifically Dependent Continuant (Quality) and SSN/SOSA:Observation. A Signal inheres in its bearer(s) — it does not exist independently. It is computed, not asserted: derived on demand from the Event log and Entity graph via a named algorithm. Domain projects define signal types, algorithms, and interpretation semantics. The Signal class captures the universal pattern: something measurable that emerges from activity, has a current value, and is recomputable from the underlying data.

invention_search.lexeme:
>-
        No vocabulary among QUDT, UCUM, ISO 80000 and the VIM cited above
        names how a source qualifies the number it states. The QUDT schema
        carries standardUncertainty and relativeStandardUncertainty, which
        quantify a measurement's dispersion rather than a source's hedge, and
        minInclusive and maxInclusive, which constrain a datatype rather than
        describe a stated bound. VIM 4.6 defines nominal quantity value as a
        rounded or approximate value characterizing a measuring instrument,
        not a reported measurement, and VIM defines no term for an
        open-ended statement. UCUM codes units and discards annotations by
        definition. ISO 80000-2 supplies the relation sign read as is
        approximately equal to, a mathematical symbol rather than a
        qualification of a reported value. The enum name and its five values
        are therefore local.
invention_search.value: No vocabulary among QUDT, UCUM, ISO 80000 and the VIM cited above names how a source qualifies the number it states. The QUDT schema carries standardUncertainty and relativeStandardUncertainty, which quantify a measurement's dispersion rather than a source's hedge, and minInclusive and maxInclusive, which constrain a datatype rather than describe a stated bound. VIM 4.6 defines nominal quantity value as a rounded or approximate value characterizing a measuring instrument, not a reported measurement, and VIM defines no term for an open-ended statement. UCUM codes units and discards annotations by definition. ISO 80000-2 supplies the relation sign read as is approximately equal to, a mathematical symbol rather than a qualification of a reported value. The enum name and its five values are therefore local.

      list is deliberately short and grows by adding values, never by

      stay exactly as the source gives them. Leaving it unset is the honest
      value when the source's form is unclear. The list is deliberately short
      and grows by adding values, never by redefining one.

value.lexeme:
>-
      A named, counted subset of the source's earthquake catalog, grouped by an
      interpretive criterion the source itself applies: a region ("beneath the
      segment RC2 axis"), a location-quality category, a depth band, or a temporal
      window. Counted's count/count_scope carries the size and the criterion in the
      source's own wording; SourceAsserted's subject links the subset to the
      GeologicalFeature it characterizes. Every other quantity the source reports
      about such a subset (a depth range, an RMS residual, an azimuthal gap, a
      magnitude, an uncertainty) is a separate Observation record whose subject is
      this record, so that one subset can carry many independently sourced
      quantities without collapsing them into one record's single quantity slot.
value.value: A named, counted subset of the source's earthquake catalog, grouped by an interpretive criterion the source itself applies: a region ("beneath the segment RC2 axis"), a location-quality category, a depth band, or a temporal window. Counted's count/count_scope carries the size and the criterion in the source's own wording; SourceAsserted's subject links the subset to the GeologicalFeature it characterizes. Every other quantity the source reports about such a subset (a depth range, an RMS residual, an azimuthal gap, a magnitude, an uncertainty) is a separate Observation record whose subject is this record, so that one subset can carry many independently sourced quantities without collapsing them into one record's single quantity slot.

            Checked BFO for a generic named-feature class: BFO's Independent
            Continuant and Site concepts are maximally generic and carry no domain
            vocabulary for a ridge segment, a transform fault, an oceanic core
            complex, or a boundary such as the brittle-ductile boundary. Checked
            SOSA/SSN's FeatureOfInterest, already considered and rejected at the
            research pack level for the same reason: it names the role a thing
            plays in one observation, not a vocabulary for the persisting seafloor
            and mantle features the source names repeatedly across many
            observations and claims. The CGI/OGC GeoSciML standard is known to
            define geologic feature and structure classes, but no version or URL
            for it could be confirmed with confidence here, so it is not cited.
            No exact term was found.

value.lexeme:
>-
      A named, spatially delimited part of the seafloor, crust, lithosphere, or
      mantle that the source repeatedly refers to and reports facts about: a ridge
      segment, a transform fault, a ridge-transform intersection, a non-transform
      discontinuity, an oceanic core complex, a detachment fault, a hydrothermal
      vent field, a volcano, or a named layer such as the crust or mantle beneath a
      given segment. Status (ACTIVE/INACTIVE/DESTROYED) captures source statements
      such as "this detachment fault is inactive" or "an extinct hydrothermal vent
      field". Distinctions the source itself draws between feature kinds are kept as
      the feature_type slot value, not as separate classes.
value.value: A named, spatially delimited part of the seafloor, crust, lithosphere, or mantle that the source repeatedly refers to and reports facts about: a ridge segment, a transform fault, a ridge-transform intersection, a non-transform discontinuity, an oceanic core complex, a detachment fault, a hydrothermal vent field, a volcano, or a named layer such as the crust or mantle beneath a given segment. Status (ACTIVE/INACTIVE/DESTROYED) captures source statements such as "this detachment fault is inactive" or "an extinct hydrothermal vent field". Distinctions the source itself draws between feature kinds are kept as the feature_type slot value, not as separate classes.

value.lexeme:
>-
      An individually identified earthquake the source names and characterizes on
      its own terms, such as the 2016 Mw 7.1 Romanche transform-fault earthquake and
      its subevents. Quantified carries its magnitude (quantity_kind e.g. "moment
      magnitude (Mw)"); Counted carries a reported subevent count where the source
      gives one; SourceAsserted's subject links it to the GeologicalFeature it is
      reported on (e.g. the Romanche transform fault). Aggregate, unnamed groups of
      earthquakes reported as statistics (a count with a depth range, an
      uncertainty, a magnitude-of-completeness) are EarthquakeCatalogSubset records,
      not SeismicEvent records, because Malleus keeps Entity and Event disjoint and
      an Observation's subject must be an Entity.
value.value: An individually identified earthquake the source names and characterizes on its own terms, such as the 2016 Mw 7.1 Romanche transform-fault earthquake and its subevents. Quantified carries its magnitude (quantity_kind e.g. "moment magnitude (Mw)"); Counted carries a reported subevent count where the source gives one; SourceAsserted's subject links it to the GeologicalFeature it is reported on (e.g. the Romanche transform fault). Aggregate, unnamed groups of earthquakes reported as statistics (a count with a depth range, an uncertainty, a magnitude-of-completeness) are EarthquakeCatalogSubset records, not SeismicEvent records, because Malleus keeps Entity and Event disjoint and an Observation's subject must be an Entity.

value.lexeme:
>-
  Project ontology for a single research article reporting a microseismicity study
  linking deep mantle earthquakes at the Mid-Atlantic Ridge (Romanche transform zone)
  to CO2 degassing from ascending melt. Domain: marine seismology, plate-boundary
  structural geology, and igneous geochemistry (MORB volatile content). Adds five
  project classes not covered by the imported packs (geological features, seismic
  events, catalog subsets, persons, organizations) and reuses the research,
  metrology, and chronology packs directly for everything else: measurements,
  claims, methods, instruments, samples, sources, evidence, and contributions.
value.value: Project ontology for a single research article reporting a microseismicity study linking deep mantle earthquakes at the Mid-Atlantic Ridge (Romanche transform zone) to CO2 degassing from ascending melt. Domain: marine seismology, plate-boundary structural geology, and igneous geochemistry (MORB volatile content). Adds five project classes not covered by the imported packs (geological features, seismic events, catalog subsets, persons, organizations) and reuses the research, metrology, and chronology packs directly for everything else: measurements, claims, methods, instruments, samples, sources, evidence, and contributions.

invention_search.lexeme:
>-
        The cited SOSA/SSN, VIM, Frascati, SEPIO, and Micropublications
        vocabularies were checked for exact generic Campaign and Instrument
        classes. SOSA/SSN uses Sensor, VIM uses measuring instrument, and no
        exact generic Campaign class was found. The accepted pack keeps the
        shorter local class names and records that choice here. CRediT names
        the fourteen roles and defines each, and ContributorRole follows its
        naming, but it is a term list with no classes, so the mixin
        Contribution and the class ContributionRelation that carry a role in a
        graph are local shapes and are recorded here. The same five
        vocabularies were checked for what a source does with a hypothesis it
        has raised. SEPIO models an assertion's evidence lines and their
        support or refutation, and Micropublications models one statement
        supporting or challenging another; both describe a relation between
        two things, not the source's own disposition of its own hypothesis.
        No term was found for it, so the enum HypothesisDisposition and the
        mixin Evaluative that marks which slots carry such a value are local
        and are recorded here. The same vocabularies were checked for what a
        record's assertion is about. SOSA/SSN defines feature of interest,
        the thing whose property an observation estimates, which fits an
        observation and not a claim, a count or an asserted ratio, and RDF 1.1
        Concepts defines subject as the position a statement is about, for
        every statement and not only a measurement. The pack borrows the RDF
        term, so subject is cited rather than invented and feature of interest
        is recorded here as the narrower term that was considered.

value.lexeme:
>-
      The entity this record's assertion is about, named as a record id that
      resolves in the same change set or the base state. Single and optional:
      a record whose subject the reading does not name leaves it unset, and
      the capture census counts it. The subject is never folded into
      quantity_kind text or into the record's own name, and it is never the
      record itself. The range is Entity, the same declaration a relation's
      endpoints carry, so what an assertion is about stays a reference to a
      thing rather than a sentence about one.

The range is Entity, the same declaration a relation's endpoints carry, so what an assertion is about stays a reference to a thing rather than a sentence about one.
